finding.summary: The new "a key's authority dies with its minter's membership" invariant is implemented twice and the two copies now disagree; the docs claim it holds for the whole v1 surface
finding.evidence: `WorkspaceScopeGuard` (workspace-scope.guard.ts:34-38) now requires `assertMember(resolvedId, user.id)` for API-key callers. `ApiV1ImageReadController` does not mount that guard (`@UseGuards(OptionalCombinedAuthGuard)`, image-read.controller.ts:41) and re-implements the check locally: `if (user?.isApiKey) { if (user.workspaceId === resolvedWorkspaceId) return; ... }` — scope match only, no membership. So the same question ("may this key act in this workspace?") gets two different answers, and the delta's own doc text is wrong: docs/design/rest-api.md:517-519 says "`WorkspaceScopeGuard` enforces the removal half for the **whole** v1 surface", and folders.controller.ts:68-74 / backend.md:293-297 make the same unqualified claim. verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is present as described. WorkspaceScopeGuard (workspace-scope.guard.ts:34-38) implements the "a key's authority dies with its minter's membership" invariant by unconditionally calling assertMember(resolvedId, Number(user.id)) after the API-key scope check, and its class doc (lines 14-20) names that as the revocation mechanism. ApiV1ImageReadController mounts only OptionalCombinedAuthGuard (image-read.controller.ts:41) — it is the sole v1 controller omitting WorkspaceScopeGuard; folders.controller.ts:39, documents.controller.ts:29, images.controller.ts:22, cells.controller.ts:31, files.controller.ts:50 and the worksheet-* controllers all mount it. Instead it re-implements the check locally at image-read.controller.ts:96-99: for user?.isApiKey it returns on bare scope equality, short-circuiting before the assertMember call at lines 102-105, which is therefore unreachable for API-key callers. api-key.strategy.ts:23-26 confirms req.user.id is the minter's createdBy, so the membership check was available and simply not made. The controller is live (api-v1.module.ts:58). The design docs assert the stricter rule without qualification: rest-api.md:522-525 says the guard "enforces the removal half for the whole v1 surface", echoed by backend.md:291-297 and folders.controller.ts:68-74. This is duplicated logic that has already diverged, giving two answers to the same authorization question, with the canonical doc wrong about the v1 surface — major under the design-fit rubric (divergent duplicate of one invariant, cost outside mere tidiness). No refutation ground applies: the code is present, reachable, and no external guard supplies the missing membership check.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. workspace-scope.guard.ts:26-40 calls assertMember unconditionally, including for API-key callers whose user.id is the minting user (api-key.strategy.ts:23), and its doc comment (lines 14-20) plus spec case (workspace-scope.guard.spec.ts:46-58) confirm the intent is that a key dies when its minter leaves the workspace. That contradicts the originating task doc's recorded decision (docs/tasks/active/20260903-api-v1-folders-copy-todo.md:49-51, "an API key acts with workspace authority ... a JWT caller is checked with isDocumentManager") and its Out-of-scope statement (lines 82-83, "Nothing here is a new capability: every endpoint's behavior already ships"), and the implementation indeed applies the manager/membership bar to API keys with no isApiKey branch (folders.controller.ts:76-86; documents.controller.ts:128-137, 175-184).
